newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Sen. Lott says tough to get budget agreement.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Sen. Lott says tough to get budget agreement.

text.p: Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said Thursday President Clinton's "unwillingness" to address the consumer price index (CPI) issue would make it difficult to reach a budget agreement.

"The president's inability or unwillingness to come up with a way to deal with the CPI problem ... has made it very tough for us to get a budget agreement of any kind because that is a significant figure and it shows to me that they're not really committed to getting a genuine balanced budget," Lott told reporters.

"The president, in my opinion, is 0 for 2 now," the Mississippi Republican said. "He did not send us a budget that showed courage and leadership, and now he has not been willing to face up to the CPI problem, he's only got one strike left," Lott said.
An advisory commission late last year headed by economist Michael Boskin said the CPI overstated inflation by about 1.1 percentage points a year.
Republicans are now likely to develop their own budget plan, Lott said. "If he doesn't get engaged with us he will become basically irrelevant in the process and we have to move on," Lott said.
He said it was now increasingly unlikely the April 15 deadline for a budget resolution would be met -- "it doesn't look very good right now."
Asked about Clinton's proposal for the District of Columbia, Lott said: "I thought it was a relatively pale proposal, but we can work with it."
